extraction.document_summary: AIA Solitaire PA (II) is a personal accident insurance plan with extended coverage beyond personal accidents. It provides 24/7 worldwide coverage for medical and other treatment costs (including TCM and chiropractic), plus coverage for items such as food poisoning and transport/building-fire related incidents. The plan is offered with 4 levels of protection (Plan 1 to Plan 4) with base benefits including Accidental Death up to S$750,000 (Plan 4), and Accidental Permanent Total Disability up to S$2,250,000 (Plan 4). It also includes Accident Medical Reimbursement with Plan 4 shown at S$5,000. Optional benefits (on top of the selected basic plan tier) include Lifestyle Maintenance (e.g., Weekly Income Benefit up to S$400) and Accidental Hospitalisation benefits (e.g., Daily Accidental Hospital Income up to S$350). A key limitation/caveat: basic coverage amounts (except the Renewal Bonus) are reduced by 50% at 75 years old, and optional benefits terminate at 75 years old; coverage is stated to be payable upon occurrence of an accident, and optional benefits have the same selected-or-lower plan type requirement.
quality_notes: The brochure clearly lists the 4 plan tiers and their base and optional benefit amounts.
No explicit exclusions were provided in the supplied text (only a general statement that exclusions exist in the policy contract).
The document does not state detailed underwriting rules beyond 'no medical check-up required'.
Benefit payout mechanics (e.g., deductibles/waiting periods, claim limits, survival periods) are not described in the supplied excerpt.

policies.quick_summary: AIA Solitaire PA (II) is AIA’s personal accident plan with worldwide coverage that extends to medical (including TCM and chiropractic), food poisoning and certain incident types (e.g., transport accidents/building fires). It has 4 protection levels (Plan 1–Plan 4) with base benefits such as Accidental Death (S$100,000 to S$750,000) and Accident Medical Reimbursement (S$2,000 to S$5,000). It also offers optional benefits for lifestyle maintenance and accidental hospitalisation. Basic benefit amounts (other than the Renewal Bonus) reduce by 50% at age 75, and optional benefits terminate at age 75.
